source_refs.note: iii) Prefix: a main subheading of 19.4 Nomenclature of Aliphatic Organic Compounds, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 41-41.

blocks.text: It gives the name of the side chain (alkyl group) or any substituent (e.g some functional group like halo, nitro, etc.) along with number of carbon atom to which it is attached.

blocks.alt: A chain of four shapes: a yellow circle 'Prefix', a blue hexagon 'Stem/Root name', a blue hexagon 'Primary Suffix (Suffix of Stem/root)' and a yellow circle 'Secondary Suffix (Suffix of F.G.)'. Arrows lead from Prefix to 'substituent and its position on the parent chain', from Stem to 'No. of carbon atoms in the parent chain', from Primary Suffix to 'saturation or unsaturation in the parent chain (an, en, yn)' and from Secondary Suffix to 'family name'.
blocks.caption: Components of a systematic (IUPAC) name (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.text: If prefix is absent, then systematic name will consist of root and suffix.

blocks.alt: Two worked examples. First: Cl-CH2-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-H with the chain carbons numbered 4, 3, 2, 1 from the left, and the name split in a box as 4-chloro | but | an | al, the parts labelled prefix, stem, suffix of stem and suffix of F.G. Second: CH3-C(CH3)=CH-CH2-OH numbered 4, 3, 2, 1, the name split as 3- methyl | but- | 2-en- | 1-ol with the same four labels.
blocks.caption: Examples: 4-chlorobutanal and 3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol, split into prefix, stem and suffixes (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The first printed example numbers a four-carbon chain but names it '4-chloro prop an al'; the stem for four carbons is 'but', so the name is 4-chlorobutanal, as drawn above.
